probableCause: The test is stale rather than the production code being wrong. StoragePolicyTest#freeStorageLasts7Days asserts 7 free days, which is the value in docs/SPEC.md. ADR-007 (Accepted 2026-03-12) supersedes that value with 10 days, and StoragePolicy.freeDays() returns 10, which matches the ADR. The SPEC section has not been updated yet, so the test most likely still encodes the outdated requirement. This is a hypothesis: the StoragePolicy source is not in the block, so the 10 is inferred from the assertion message only.
evidence: Assertion failure: "expected: <7> but was: <10>" at StoragePolicyTest.java:14, where the code is assertEquals(7, policy.freeDays()).
docs/adr/ADR-007-free-storage-days.md: "The free storage period at the destination port is 10 days... The fee starts on the 11th day." Status: Accepted on 2026-03-12.
ADR-007 states that it "Supersedes the value of 7 days in the 'Storage fees' section of docs/SPEC.md, which has not been updated yet."
ADR-007 Consequences: "Code and tests must use 10 days."
docs/SPEC.md 'Storage fees' still says 7 days free and charges from the 8th day, which is the outdated value the test reflects.
The other test in the class, storageBeyondTheFreePeriodIsCharged, asserts assertFalse(policy.isFree(11)), which is consistent with a 10-day free period and the fee starting on day 11.

possibleSolutions.solution: Update the test to match ADR-007: rename it to something like freeStorageLasts10Days and assert 10 for policy.freeDays(). Consider also covering the boundary with assertTrue(policy.isFree(10)).
tradeoffs: Aligns the test with the accepted decision and is a small change.
Requires a human to confirm that StoragePolicy.freeDays() really returns 10 intentionally and not by accident.
Renaming the test changes its identity in CI history and reports.

possibleSolutions.solution: Correct the 'Storage fees' section of docs/SPEC.md to 10 days free and the fee from the 11th day, in the same change as the test update.
tradeoffs: Removes the contradiction between SPEC and ADR that caused the stale test.
Expands the scope of the change beyond the test, although the ADR already plans this in the next documentation pass.

possibleSolutions.solution: Investigative step: open StoragePolicy and its history to confirm freeDays() returns 10 and was changed in line with ADR-007 before changing the test.
tradeoffs: Verifies the hypothesis, since the production source is not in the evidence.
Costs a little extra review time.

possibleSolutions.solution: Do not revert the production code to 7 days to make the test pass.
tradeoffs: Reverting would make the test green but contradict the accepted ADR-007 and the negotiated terms with the shipping lines.
Only reasonable if the ADR is shown to be withdrawn, and no evidence of that is present.

confidenceReason: The failing assertion (7 vs 10) matches exactly the conflict between the outdated SPEC value and the accepted ADR-007, which explicitly supersedes it and says tests must use 10 days. The remaining uncertainty is that the StoragePolicy source is not shown.
limitations: The StoragePolicy source is not included, so the value 10 is inferred from the assertion message and not read from the code.
